Beyond the questions of how it will explain away the absences of Sam and Tara Carpenter, played by Melissa Barrera and Jenna Ortega, one of the biggest mysteries is once more the identity of Ghostface. The Scream movies have always had clever reveals with the killer's identity, and the theories around Ghostface's plot in Scream 7 have been especially prominent with the confirmed returns of dead characters : Stu Macher (Matthew Lillard), Roman Bridger (Scott Foley), and Dewey Riley (David Arquette). The Scream 7 trailer stops short of unmasking Ghostface to not spoil the movie's biggest twists, but there are a few hints about who is under the iconic mask. Based on multiple different developments, Stu may very well be Ghostface in Scream 7 . "Reminds Me Of Where We Grew Up" One of the earliest teases of this new Ghostface's identity comes during what plays as their first conversation with Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell) on the phone. The killer talks about the small town where she now lives and the beautiful daughter she has (more on her later). Then, there's the notable line, "Reminds me of where we grew up." While the killer could be lying and not really be from Woodsboro, California, that is where the phone call originates from on the caller ID. This increases the likelihood that Scream 7 's Ghostface killer a) grew up in Woodsboro and b) grew up there with Sidney. That limits the pool of possibilities in terms of known characters from the franchise. Gale Weathers (Courteney Cox) and Randy Meeks (Jamie Kennedy) are the only major ones still alive, other than Sidney. But, Gale certainly is not going to be the killer at this point, and Randy is not returning, as far as we know. With Dewey and Stu returning in some form, that turns the attention toward them more so. Stu would make more sense, as his "death" is much easier to undo than Dewey's. He also would have the motive, to finish what he and Billy Loomis started all those years ago and get revenge on Sidney for smashing his face with a TV. So, if Scream 7 's Ghostface killer is someone who grew up with Sidney in Woodsboro, Stu would fit that bill. Sidney's Daughter's Name Connects Her To Stu Stu Macher (Matthew Lillard) and Tatum Riley (Rose McGowan) in Scream 1996 The Scream 7 trailer also revealed a major new detail about the franchise that holds a connection to Stu. The movie introduces Sidney's daughter, played by Isabel May. It's confirmed in the trailer that Sidney named her daughter Tatum , which is the same name as her best friend in the original film. Rose McGowan played Tatum Riley in the 1996 movie. She was directly connected to most of the main characters in the film. Tatum was Sidney's best friend, explaining why she would give her daughter this name. She is also Dewey's sister, which notably adds another connection to Arquette's character for his mysterious return. Scream 7 naming Sidney's daughter Tatum also connects her to Stu, as Tatum Riley was his girlfriend. This adds another layer of creepiness to his line about Sidney's "beautiful daughter" and could even help explain why she is so important to Ghostface's plan. Stu may view her as a reminder of the relationship he lost as part of his and Billy's scheme. After all, the movie could have named Sidney's daughter anything. Choosing Tatum specifically had to be done for a reason. And if Stu is the killer, then bringing in this connection would make sense for the overall story, rather than just have the teenager's name be a reference to an original character. Burning Down The Macher House Ghostface burning down the Macher house in Scream 7 It's also notable that there is a heavy emphasis on the Macher house in Scream 7 based on the trailer. It begins with a return to the residence, which is now an Airbnb filled with connections to the original murders, Ghostface, and the in-universe Stab movies. The Macher house was a central location in the original film, as it was Stu's home, and most recently returned in the end of 2022's Scream . It appears that after Amber Freeman's (Mikey Madison) death and everything that happened at the residence, her parents sold the property, or morbidly turned it into an Airbnb themselves. In any case, the presence of the Macher house brings a direct connection to Stu. The Ghostface killer wanting to "burn it all to the ground" and literally set the house on fire could be telling. No one else would likely care as much that the house had been transformed it into a place that is benefiting from the deaths that occurred. Other than just having a sense of theatrics, it wouldn't really make sense for someone else to want to burn the Macher house down. But if Stu is Ghostface, then there are plenty of reasons why he'd want to destroy his childhood home and some of the lasting memories of what happened decades ago. "This Is Going To Be Fun" Ghostface in Scream 7 While all the previous points help point to Stu, some could still be seen as hints to other Ghostface reveals. But the trailer certainly wants audiences to be thinking about one half of the franchise's original killer reveal. This is evident by letting us hear Matthew Lillard's voice at the very end, as Stu says, "This is going to be fun." This is unmistakably the voice of Stu without any modulations from a voice changer. Using him as the last bit of audio in the trailer is a way to tease how large his role is in the film without directly confirming anything. Think of how Lucasfilm used Palpatine's laughter at the end of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker 's first trailer. This time, it's Stu who has somehow returned . The context for Stu's line is unknown, so there is always a chance that this was done intentionally to throw audiences off from the true nature of his role and the actual identity of the Ghostface killer. That would be easier to believe if there weren't so many connections to Stu sprinkled throughout the trailer, increasing the likelihood that he's back as Ghostface in Scream 7 . text: British designer with punk-rock take on fashion, Pam Hogg, dies | News Friday 28 November, 2025 Archive বাংলা HOME News Chief Adviser's News 100 Days of Interim Government President Top News National July Uprising Arts & Entertainment Education News Health News Climate Change & Environment Science & Technology Weather Business International District Festival of Youth 2025 Sports Subscriber NOTICE News Flash Pakistan's PM, FM send bouquets praying for Khaleda Zia's recovery Govt brings Rohingya crisis back to global forum: Shafiqul EC seeks full cooperation to ensure fair, peaceful election Instruction given to arrest attackers on Baul artistes immediately: Shafiqul Alam Draft of human trafficking prevention ordinance gets final approval News BSS 27 Nov 2025, 08:28 British designer with punk-rock take on fashion, Pam Hogg, dies LONDON, Nov 27, 2025 (BSS/AFP) - Fashion designer Pam Hogg, known for her punk rock, non-conformist creations who dressed stars such as Rihanna and Lady Gaga, has died, her family announced on Wednesday. Hogg was an iconic figure of London fashion week with her futuristic looks, daring hairstyles and flamboyant outfits that mixed irony, feminism and counter-culture at her catwalk shows. Announcing her death on social media, the Scottish designer's family said her "creative spirit and body of work touched the lives of many people of all ages". "She leaves a magnificent legacy that will continue to inspire, bring joy and challenge us to live beyond the confines of convention," they said in a statement, accompanied by a photo of the designer, dressed in gold and white and wearing her signature red lipstick. While not revealing the cause of death, the family thanked staff at a hospice in east London, saying Hogg died surrounded by friends and family. They did not give her age -- which she had always kept under wraps -- but the Guardian newspaper believed her to be aged 66. Tributes have been paid including by actresses Rose McGowan and Patricia Arquette, the band Blondie and designer Roksanda Ilincic. Born in the Scottish town of Paisley, known for its textiles industry, Hogg studied in the city of Glasgow and at London's Royal College of Art. She unveiled her first collection in 1981 and was often compared to Vivienne Westwood, another queen of British punk-rock culture, who died in 2022. Kate Moss and Beyonce were also among the stars to have worn Hogg's designs. In the video for her 2007 song "2 Hearts", Kylie Minogue wore a black, metal-studded catsuit by the designer. Hogg also played in several bands, including Doll, which opened for Debbie Harry in the 1990s. The franchise’s ultimate final girl missed out on the sixth installment, as contract negotiations with Campbell fell through, but she’s back for number seven, and once again the target of Ghostface. As the Scream 7 trailer makes clear, Sid is going to be dragged back to her past battles in Woodsboro by the latest iteration of the killer, and it promises to be one of her most personal fights with him to date. Videos by ComicBook.com This time around, it isn’t just Sidney who Ghostface is trying to kill , but the rest of her family – there’s her husband, Mark (Joel McHale), and even more notably her daughter, played by Isabel May. The first trailer revealed a bittersweet connection between Sidney’s daughter and the franchise’s history by confirming that she’s called Tatum, named after Sid’s best friend and Dewey Riley’s sister from the first movie, who was played by Rose McGowan. That Tatum had one of Scream ‘s most memorable deaths, as she was crushed by a garage door while stuck in a cat flap, but Sidney has made sure to honor her friend – and now has to hope her daughter can escape a similar fate. Tatum Makes Scream 7 Worse For Sidney Prescott The inclusion of Tatum as a target for Ghostface makes this latest round with the masked serial killer so much worse for Sidney. It’s her greatest fear come to life: that not only will she once again be the main focus of their murderous plans, but that her family will be as well. And her daughter being named after her friend only compounds the issue and brings with it a sense of things coming full circle, as what was intended to honor her now becomes a harrowing reminder of the last time Ghostface went after a Tatum. Play video However, while May’s character carries the name Tatum, the trailer also suggests she’ll very much take after her mother. She even wears the same jacket that Sid did in Scream 2 , and says she wants to be a “fighter,” like her mom, echoing words directly spoken by Sidney previously in the franchise. Tatum isn’t backing down from Ghostface, but is prepared to take the fight to him in a similar way, setting up what will presumably be the final girl s of the movie. Read Next Every Ghostface Killer in Scream, Ranked Of course, Sidney is no stranger to her family being involved in Ghostface affairs – though it’s often been on the other side. Her half-brother, Roman Bridger, was the killer in Scream 3 (and will be back in some way in the seventh installment), and her cousin, Jill Roberts, was one of the murderers in Scream 4 . It’s probably safe to assume that twist won’t be repeated, and there’ll be no Tatum-as-Ghostface reveal, although I guess you never fully know with this franchise. Even without that, though, there’s plenty of Sidney’s past coming back to haunt her. As mentioned, Roman will return in some capacity, and so too will Stu Macher . The new Ghostface, whomever it is, refers to “where we grew up,” and the trailer shows the Macher house burning down, so there’s clearly a strong connection to the franchise’s past and to Sidney’s entire life here, from her days in Woodsboro with Tatum Riley to her days as a mother with Tatum, her daughter, and it’s all going to collide in horrifying fashion. Scream 7 will be released on February 27th, 2026. What do you think? Leave a comment below and join the conversation now in the ComicBook Forum ! According to Variety , while addressing the crowd, Lillard urged compassion and community in his remarks before punctuating his message with a clear statement: “F*** ICE,” he said. “In this time, in this city, we need to lead with love. Do not forget that s*** in this moment. Not to be political, but to be political as s***.” Matthew Lillard Lillard’s comments drew applause from attendees and quickly spread online, where fans praised his outspokenness. The Scream and Scooby-Doo star joins a growing number of Hollywood figures who have publicly criticized ICE policies and practices in recent years. Actors including Mark Ruffalo and Jamie Lee Curtis have previously spoken out on the issue, calling for accountability and compassion in U.S. immigration enforcement. Ruffalo described ICE as “stamping their boots on your right to a fair trial,” while Curtis reposted videos of alleged abuses with the caption “why?” Lillard’s comments highlight how political and social consciousness continues to intersect with Hollywood’s horror icons. Decades after first playing Scream ’s infamous killer, the actor remains vocal about the real-world horrors he believes deserve equal attention. The original “Hocus Pocus” was released in 1993 and quickly became a cult classic. Thora Birch’s Interest in Dani’s Fate During a recent appearance, Birch shared her enthusiasm about reprising her role. She indicated that she would like to explore how her character has evolved since the iconic Halloween night depicted in the first film. Birch stated, “I’d like to know what they land on for how Dani wound up. I’m super open to the idea.” Return of Beloved Characters The original “Hocus Pocus” featured several key characters aside from Dani. These included: Max, played by Omri Katz Allison, portrayed by Vinessa Shaw Zombie Billy Butcherson, played by Doug Jones Although these characters did not appear in “Hocus Pocus 2,” Birch’s interest raises questions about their potential return in the next film. Excitement for Hocus Pocus 3 Fans are eagerly awaiting updates on “Hocus Pocus 3.” Last week, Bette Midler, who reprises her role as Winifred Sanderson, mentioned that she has already read the script. She described much of it as “brilliant,” heightening anticipation for the upcoming sequel. As the production moves forward, it remains to be seen how the directors will weave together the stories of both returning characters and newcomers. Pictures By Federico Furzan Published Nov 1, 2025 Federico is a writer and journalist who joined the MovieWeb family a few years ago, bringing in his years-long experience as a critic of all kinds of films, especially indies. He's had the fortune of being part of several initiatives on the site. He's one of the hounds catching breaking news from the other side of the world, and always on the lookout for upcoming streaming releases (especially within the horror spectrum). At the moment, Federico is focusing on writing articles for the News and Features team, but you can find his insight on lists that mostly focus on '80s cinema, classic horror, and true crime. Before joining MovieWeb, he navigated as a blogger, and eventually, found himself becoming a film critic. You can read some of his reviews on Rotten Tomatoes. Sign in to your MovieWeb account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 4 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Zack Snyder's 2011 fantasy action thriller Sucker Punch is one of his most controversial and divisive movies. Discourse around the film has continued more or less unabated since it arrived in theaters — and now it's landed at a new streaming home, giving everyone a chance to revisit (and possibly re-evaluate) it. As of November 1, as part of the network's monthly update, it's on HBO Max . Starring Emily Browning, Abbie Cornish, and Jena Malone, among many others, Sucker Punch was critically panned when originally released. It didn't do well at the box office either, grossing less than $90 million against its $82 million budget. Snyder rebounded, however; his next release, 2013's Man of Steel , officially started his run in the DCEU (or the Snyderverse, as his most loyal fans like to call it). In Sucker Punch , a young woman is framed by her stepfather for the murder of her sister. She's sent to a psychiatric hospital, were her stepfather finds a way to have her lobotomized. She descends into a fantasy realm where she acquires the name Babydoll and meets a gang of female warriors. Joining forces, they resolve to do everything in their power to escape. Per the Rotten Tomatoes synopsis: Locked away, a young woman named Babydoll (Emily Browning) retreats to a fantasy world where she is free to go wherever her mind takes her. Determined to fight for real freedom, she finds four women – Rocket, Blondie, Amber and Sweet Pea – to join together to escape the terrible fate that awaits them. With a virtual arsenal at their disposal, the allies battle everything from samurais to serpents, while trying to decide what price they will pay for survival. Does 'Sucker Punch' Deserve a Re-Evaluation? Carla Gugino and Emily Browning in Sucker Punch Warner Bros. Pictures Sucker Punch was released the same year audiences flocked to theaters to see Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 , Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol , and Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides , among others. The ten highest-grossing films of the year were sequels, franchise entries, or were inspired by a previous property. Original films like Sucker Punch didn't stand a chance of becoming wildly successful audience favorites, a trend that has persisted to this day. The critical reception was also ghastly — it's Snyder's lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes, alongside his two Rebel Moon movies. Though the director isn't known for being a favorite among critics, the disdain toward Sucker Punch is particularly vehement. Famed critic Roger Ebert was one of many who hated the movie, writing this in his capsule review on Twitter: " Sucker Punch is so bad when the lobotomist turned up Peter Sobczynski wanted to scream 'I'll have what she's having!'" Even though Sucker Punch isn't a perfect movie, in retrospect, it might be better than critics and audiences thought back in the day. Some people will argue that he's a visionary director who's been unfairly maligned by critics and the Internet. Others feel his work is juvenile at best and, at worst, incredibly self-indulgent. Most of this discussion stems from the fact that Snyder's work often adapts pre-existing material, whether it's iconic comics like Watchmen and 300 or mythology in his Netflix series Twilight of the Gods . It's Snyder's first original film, Sucker Punch , that is receiving a new lease on life , breaking into the Top 10 on HBO Max this week , per FlixPatrol . Looking at any of the trailers or stills from Sucker Punch , it's not hard to see why it's a draw for HBO Max users. The film follows Babydoll ( Emily Browning ), a young woman who is falsely institutionalized for the murder of her sister. Intending to escape before she's lobotomized, she turns to the other patients for help: Rocket ( Jena Malone ) and her sister Sweet Pea ( Abbie Cornish ), Amber ( Jamie Chung ), and "Blondie" ( Vanessa Hudgens ). The five women embark on a journey through different fantasy worlds full of stone samurai, a train full of killer robots, and steam-powered Nazi zombies. If that wasn't enough, Babydoll also fantasizes that she and her newfound friends are dancers in a brothel, which looks and sounds like a hyper-stylized and hyper-violent take on Inception . It also bears all of Snyder's signature flourishes, including slo-mo fight scenes and visuals that tend to have more definition than the characters, so what went wrong the first time around? Zack Snyder Has Yet To Realize His True Vision for ‘Sucker Punch’ When Sucker Punch had its theatrical release in 2011, it was a critical punching bag and a box office bomb. Quentin Tarantino scathingly referred to it as " one of the worst films of 2011 ", while other reviews compared it to a bad video game despite Snyder's insistence he didn't want the film to play out like one . Yet Babydoll and her friends are sent on quests to find various items, hoping to achieve a "perfect victory" that sounds more like a video game. The kicker was the fate of the main characters; nearly all the main heroines are brutally killed or maimed, which didn't earn the film any favors . Yet as time has passed, Sucker Punch has gathered a cult following and has even been examined through the lens of satire . There might be an underlying reason Sucker Punch received such a poor reception: it's not the version of the film Snyder intended to show the world . While Sucker Punch would receive a director's cut in the vein of other Snyder films , he told Empire Magazine in an interview last year that he'd like the chance to re-edit the film to match his vision : "I have the footage already shot: they just have to let me put it together...We ask every now and then. We have to ask again. I think there has to be a window when no-one’s got the movie." Given that Snyder was eventually able to complete his version of Justice League , there's a possibility that lightning could strike twice in his favor. However, it all comes down to whether Warner Bros. Pictures is willing to pull the trigger and whether there's a similar demand for the "Snyder Cut" of Sucker Punch. Posts By Marcel Ardivan Apr 11, 2025 ‘Sucker Punch’ Was a Major Stepping Stone for One Actor Everett Collection One of the most impressive aspects of Sucker Punch , aside from its gorgeous visuals, is its stacked ensemble cast . In addition to the main heroines, Sucker Punch also features Jon Hamm , Carla Gugino , and Oscar Isaac in key roles. In the case of Isaac, he portrays Blue Jones, the main antagonist of Sucker Punch. Isaac's performance allows him to craft two different characters, as Blue's depicted as the owner of a brothel and a domineering orderly at the asylum; both are equally slimy. Isaac is often considered one of the best parts of Sucker Punch , and, thanks to that film and his appearance in Drive , 2011 was his breakout year, leading him to bigger and better performances, including Guillermo del Toro 's Frankenstein . Sucker Punch, in many ways, best defines Zack Snyder as a filmmaker . It is visually stunning and swings for the fences, but it is also extremely divisive. Now that it's made the top 10 charts on HBO Max, a whole new audience will have the chance to decide whether it's a misunderstood masterpiece or a major misfire. Facebook Instagram Twitter TikTok YouTube Subscribe Search Language English Español Entertainment 3 New-to-HBO Max Movies I Can’t Wait to Watch This Weekend (November 7-9) By Jason Struss November 7, 2025 TOP STORIES Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Tom Hanks in A Man Called Otto Niko Tavernise / © Sony Pictures Entertainment / Courtesy Everett Collection Tap Here To Add Us Weekly As A Trusted Source Add as a preferred source on Google HBO Max is the place to be if you want to watch buzzy movies like Weapons and Materialists , but it also has some films you might not have seen or heard about. Watch With Us is here to highlight three overlooked HBO Max movies that are worth your time this weekend. If you’re a fan of Tom Hanks , you should check out A Man Called Otto, a 2022 drama that features one of his best performances. History meets horror in the irreverent comedy Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter , while Sucker Punch delivers the kind of action thrills you expect from director Zack Snyder . ‘A Man Called Otto’ (2022) Otto Anderson ( Tom Hanks ) is a 63-year-old widower who doesn’t like life that much. He’s still mourning his late wife, while his forced retirement leaves him with nothing to do but contemplate his own suicide. His life is shaken up by the arrival of his new neighbors, Marisol ( Mariana Treviño ) and Tommy ( Manuel Garcia-Rulfo ), who slowly begin to thaw Otto’s ice-cold heart. As he slowly comes out of his shell, Otto remembers the good times he spent with his wife and wonders if he has any left without her. Related: 6 New Movies to Watch This Weekend on Netflix, Prime Video and More (November 21-23) It’s the weekend before Thanksgiving, and streamers like Netflix, HBO Max and Hulu are dishing out a digital feast of some of the best new movies around. Netflix has two notable movies worth streaming: Train Dreams, a poetic drama that will probably be nominated for a few Oscars, and Champagne Problems, a holiday rom-com that […] A Man Called Otto walks a tricky line between a depressing drama about a suicidal man and a sickly sweet sentimental movie about a cranky man who transforms into someone lovable. It works because of Hanks, who doesn’t ask for his audience’s sympathy but earns it. His Otto is impossible to deal with, but he subtly reveals why his wife stayed with him for all those years. Somewhere beneath his scowls, Otto is a good person, and it’s a credit to Hanks that he shows him at his best and at his worst. A Man Called Otto is streaming on HBO Max. ‘Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter’ (2012) HBO Max was a little late adding Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter on November 1, but just because Halloween is over doesn’t make the film any less fun to watch. Less scary and more comedic, the horror satire stars Benjamin Walker as America’s 16th president, who started as an idealistic lawyer and, yes, vampire hunter. He teams up with the mysterious Henry Sturges ( Dominic Cooper ) to take down Adam ( Rufus Sewell ), a master vampire who is using the slave trade to grow his undead army. Determined to abolish both slavery and creatures of the night, Lincoln perfects his fighting skills while rising in power as a masterful politician. Believe it or not, Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter is actually a pretty faithful retelling of Lincoln’s life and career, minus all the vampire bits. And it’s fun to watch how the movie embellishes fact with supernatural fiction, like how Confederate President Jefferson Davis recruits vampires (!) during the Civil War to fight the Union. It’s that kind of movie, but it’s an action romp that’s intentionally stylish and nutty. If you ever wanted to relive American history, there are worse ways to do it. Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter is streaming on HBO Max. ‘Sucker Punch’ (2011) Sometimes, you need to see a movie that’s pure adolescent fantasy, and who better to deliver that than Zack Snyder? The 300 director has made a career at fulfilling the dreams of immature 12-year-old boys, and it doesn’t get more ridiculously over the top than in Sucker Punch , a mishmash of fantasy, cyberpunk and exploitation movie designed as a feminist call-to-arms for all the badass gals in the audience – and the boys who lust after them. If you’ve just finished Reacher and you’re looking for your next dose of adrenaline, Amazon Prime Video has you covered. Tom Clancy’s Jack Ryan is the kind of show that grabs you by the collar from the first episode and doesn’t let go. Blending intelligence work , international intrigue, and heart-stopping action, it’s a masterclass in how to make a political thriller both thrilling and deeply human. At the centre of it all is John Krasinski – yes, the same actor you once knew as the affable Jim from The Office . Here, though, he’s swapped the jokes for a bulletproof vest, stepping into the role of CIA analyst Jack Ryan. What starts as a desk job quickly spirals into a series of dangerous field missions spanning the globe—from Middle Eastern deserts to the streets of Washington. From analyst to action hero Developed by Carlton Cuse and Graham Roland , the show reimagines Tom Clancy’s classic hero for the modern age. Jack Ryan begins as a man of numbers and intelligence reports – the kind of analyst who prefers spreadsheets to gunfire. But when his financial data uncovers a pattern that points to a major terrorist plot, he’s forced out of the office and straight into the chaos of fieldwork. Each season plunges Ryan into a different corner of global conflict – think geopolitical drama , high-stakes espionage, and the kind of moral dilemmas that make you question who the “good guys” really are. The tone is intense yet grounded, the kind of storytelling that keeps you watching long after you should have gone to bed. A cast that keeps the tension alive The series benefits from a strong supporting cast, including Wendell Pierce , Abbie Cornish , Noomi Rapace , and Michael Kelly . Each brings something vital to the mix – loyalty, mystery, grit – and together they create a web of relationships that feel as real as the missions themselves. The one-camera style of shooting adds to the realism, giving the action sequences a raw, almost documentary edge. Episodes typically run 40-60 minutes, and each season serves as a contained story while still following Jack’s professional and emotional evolution. Whether he’s unravelling corruption in Venezuela or preventing an international crisis, the tension never lets up. A show that just gets better Interestingly, Jack Ryan didn’t start as a critical darling. The first season earned a solid 75% rating on Rotten Tomatoes , respectable but not stellar. By season four, however, that score had climbed to 94% , a testament to how the show found its rhythm over time. Critics have praised its refined pacing, stronger character development, and more cohesive storytelling in later seasons. It’s a rare thing these days – a show that not only sustains its momentum but actually improves with each new chapter. By the final season, the stakes are higher, the writing sharper, and Krasinski’s performance more nuanced than ever. Why fans of Reacher will love it Like Reacher , this series delivers a perfect mix of muscle and mind . There’s plenty of action for thrill-seekers – car chases, shootouts, and close calls aplenty – but it’s grounded in thoughtful storytelling and political realism. It’s not just about saving the world; it’s about understanding it. Yes, there are moments when the plot leans into the spectacular, or when coincidences stretch credibility – but that’s part of the fun. For every over-the-top sequence, there’s a quiet, tense exchange in a dimly lit office that reminds you this isn’t just a blockbuster – it’s a story about the people behind the missions. If you’re craving a smart, high-octane thriller that balances action with intelligence, Jack Ryan is the one to add to your watchlist. By the time you reach the end of episode one, you’ll understand why so many viewers call it one of the best spy dramas on Amazon. 0 0 Total 0 Shares Share 0 Tweet 0 Pin it 0 Share 0 Share 0 Share 0 Talk Android Author Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. Zach has had articles published on satirical sites such as Points In Case, Slackjaw, and McSweeney's. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap If you love horror, you owe it to yourself to watch HBO's Lovecraft Country , a fantastic series with an 88% on Rotten Tomatoes . Horror fans have been eating well this last decade on streaming television, with a lot of horror hits coming out on Netflix, HBO, and Amazon Prime Video. HBO Max, in particular, has been bringing the scares . The Last of Us , True Blood , The Outsider , and now It: Welcome to Derry are all massively popular TV shows and great examples of how to do long-form horror. Lovecraft Country should be added to this list as well. Lovecraft Country Is A Horrifying, Entertaining Series Lovecraft Country is a wildly unique horror series, and while it does include some of the mind-melting beasts courtesy of the show's namesake, like shoggoths and Cthulu, it's not an adaptation of any one H.P. story. Instead, it's an adaptation of Matt Ruff's 2016 horror novel. The series is set in 1950s Jim Crow America and follows Tic Freeman (Jonathan Majors) and Leti Lewis (Jurnee Smollett) as they embark on a dangerous road trip through some of the most racist parts of the country. They meet horrors beyond their comprehension, and bring them back to Chicago with them. While the monsters, witches, and ghosts are plenty terrifying, it's the violent racism they face day in and day out that puts them most at peril. Lovecraft Country is a beautifully directed show with fantastical ideas mixed in elegantly with the issues of segregation and prejudice, making for a terrifying and thoughtful experiment. Lovecraft Country Was Canceled After One Season Despite Great Reviews Lovecraft Country ran for 10 episodes, and it felt like the series had plenty of ideas for more seasons to come, but in July 2021, HBO announced that they were canceling the series (via Deadline ). HBO simply said, " We will not be moving forward with a second season of Lovecraft Country ." While Lovecraft Country season 1 had a book to go off, showrunner Misha Green and her team had to craft an original story for season 2. It sounds like HBO gave Green and her team some time to think up a new season, but ultimately decided that they would be canceling the show instead. Lovecraft Country was slow to grow, but once it did, it had significant viewing numbers. The season finale hit a viewership high with 1.5 M, becoming the most-watched new episode of an HBO Max original series in its first day. While it's sad there will be no more new episodes, Lovecraft Country season 1 is still worth the watch. 9.0 /10 7 /10 Lovecraft Country 10 stars 9 stars 8 stars 7 stars 6 stars 5 stars 4 stars 3 stars 2 stars 1 star Like Follow Followed Drama Mystery Sci-Fi & Fantasy Horror Release Date 2020 - 2020-00-00 Network HBO Showrunner Misha Green Cast See All Courtney B. The “Westworld” actress made a cameo at the star-studded event in Los Angeles on Thursday night, hitting the red carpet in a black oversize Palomo skirt suit and white pumps. Her understated heels hailed from Jude, an emerging shoe brand launched last year by Jurgita Dileviciute and Denitsa Bumbarova, both of whom have backgrounds in designing footwear and accessories. Per Jude’s website, each pair is made in Portugal using premium Italian and French leathers. Thompson opted for the up-and-coming label’s Fame silhouette, which featured a 105mm stiletto heel, pointed toe and low-cut vamp, accentuating the foot’s arch. Retailing for $550, the shoes come in a wide range of colors and finishes, running the gamut from brown croc-embossed to khaki suede. FilmMagic Thompson was outfitted in a roomy black blazer with structured shoulder pads from Palomo’s spring 2026 collection, which debuted on the runway during Madrid Fashion Week in September. She wore the jacket sans shirt, instead revealing a sliver of her black bra underneath. The slouchy piece was balanced with a matching midi skirt, which was much more fitted. A thick white choker added a playful element to the luxe black-and-white ensemble. Thompson’s hair was pulled back in an updo, showcasing her glowy, soft makeup. The annual gala, a fundraising event held by Women In Film, also drew in stars like Regina King, who wore a Max Mara denim suit from its Sportmax collection, Jurnee Smollett, also in Max Mara, Felicity Jones and Maude Apatow. On Friday night, Nicky Zimmermann and Simone Zimmermann hosted a star-studded dinner at Chateau Marmont to celebrate the Australian brand’s cruise 2026 collection, “Twisted Romance.” The new collection is inspired by “nostalgia, femininity, and the fantasy of escape,” and the glamorous celebration reflected the same feeling. Guests, including Zoey Deutch, Jurnee Smollett, and Emma Roberts, were treated to a candlelit dinner in the famed hotel’s Bungalow, at tables set with antique candelabras, strings of pearls, and lush greenery. Stefanie Keenan // Getty Images Emma Roberts before dinner. Following dinner, guests headed upstairs to the Chateau Marmont’s Penthouse for dancing and continued festivities, complete with a set by DJ Kitty Kash. WWD // Getty Images DJ Kitty Kash manning the turntable. “Cruise 26 is inspired by nostalgic pirate adventures and the flamboyance of the New Romantics,” said Nicky in a statement on the new collection. “A treasure trove of nostalgia is given fresh interpretation through fluid fabrics, dynamic shapes and illustrative prints to capture a carefree mood.” The creative director continued, “We played a lot with contrast—floaty silks against structured denim, delicate lace paired with sharp tailoring. There’s volume, romance, and drama, but it’s never too serious. That tension is what makes it feel modern: celebrating a sense of fun, freedom and a little rebellious adventure.” Stefanie Keenan // Getty Images Nina Garcia and Bella Heathcote. The invite list included some of the biggest names in Hollywood, all of them wearing pieces from the collection, including Dakota Fanning, Rita Ora, Halle Bailey, Delaney Rowe, Isabela Merced, Bella Heathcote, Maria Bakalova, Abby Champion, and more. Getty Images for Zimmermann The sandal, which retails for $975, is set with four straps that buckle across the foot and ankle. Rope work, drawstring volume and hardware-driven accessories run through the collection, reflecting the brand’s ongoing footwear development between its Sydney and Paris ateliers. A closer look at Rita Ora’s Zimmerman Orla Buckle Sandals . Getty Images for Zimmermann Ora paired the sandal with a two-piece white set, also from Zimmermann’s resort 2026 collection, that featured rope ties at the neck and waist. The top used knotted halter straps and wide gathered panels through the sleeves and bodice. A matching skirt continued the construction with cinched pleating and rope that crossed the torso before looping through the upper skirt seam. A week later in Paris, she wore Giuseppe Zanotti’s Sylvy platforms at the Balenciaga Dinner — a patent style with a covered block heel and rounded platform. Earlier this month in London, she shifted to satin with Russell & Bromley’s Hillcliffe slingbacks for the Music Industry Trust Awards. Zimmermann Orla Buckle Sandal in Moss, $975. text: 'Masterpiece' crime drama has TV fans completely 'hooked' after just one season - The Mirror ‌ ‌ Skip to main content News Celebs Football Lifestyle More InYourArea Funeral Notices Shop Competitions Dating Offers Newsletter Signup Follow us on social Daily Mirror Icon TV TV News Apple TV 'Masterpiece' crime drama has TV fans completely 'hooked' after just one season All nine episodes of the first season of this 'haunting' crime drama are available to stream now and fans are already desperate for a second season to binge-watch Comments TV Emily Malia GAU Writer 14:28, 29 Oct 2025 Updated 14:29, 29 Oct 2025 View 2 Images The gripping series is loosely based on the crimes of a notorious American arsonist (Image: AP) Released earlier this year in June 2025, the crime drama 'Smoke' has had TV fans glued to their screens, completely engrossed in the nine gripping episodes of this investigative tale. ‌ Featuring Welsh actor Taron Egerton as the lead character Dave Goodsen, 'Smoke' is an American crime drama that trails a detective and an arson investigator on the hunt for two serial fire-starters. The show's premise is inspired by the popular true crime podcast 'Firebug', which delves into the actions of notorious arsonist John Leonard Orr. ‌ Goodsen, a former firefighter, transitioned into an arson investigator following a distressing incident that led him to retire from his initial role. As two criminals begin setting fires across the region and he struggles to keep pace with their antics, a police officer named Michelle Calderon, portrayed by Jurnee Smollett , steps in to assist the investigation. ‌ The intriguing storyline unfolds in the Pacific Northwest in the US, where the officer is determined to redeem herself in the force after being demoted due to an affair with her captain. She's keen to nab the culprits to prove her worth once more, but her personal life becomes increasingly complex as the investigation progresses. View 2 Images Taron Egerton and Jurnee Smollett in Smoke (Image: Apple) A fan of Smoke wrote on Rotten Tomatoes: "What an absolute knockout of a series. Smoke is one of those rare shows that combines grit, atmosphere, and emotional intensity into a slow-burn story that never lets up." ‌ They added on the show's production: "The cinematography alone is breathtaking - every frame feels deliberate, moody, and artfully layered, drawing you right into its haunting tone. The writing is sharp, unpredictable, and unafraid to explore the darker edges of human nature." However, what they couldn't resist highlighting was the display from the lead performer, most famous for his part in The Kingsman. They said: "But what truly elevates this show is Taron Egerton's phenomenal performance. "He's magnetic-balancing vulnerability, intensity, and complexity in a way few actors can." This viewer wasn't alone in expressing their admiration for the show's cast. ‌ Another said: "Slow to get going, but the acting is superb. For fans of Taron Egerton, it's great to see him play such a different role! Well worth the watch." The remaining ensemble features Hollywood star Greg Kinnear portraying Commander Harvey Englehart alongside Rafe Spall as Captain Steven Burke and Hannah Emily Anderson as Ashley Gudsen. Numerous viewers have commended the complete cast, describing the performances as "top-notch", whilst acknowledging it required patience to fully engage with the series. One Smoke fan expressed their surprise at how much they enjoyed the show's unique concept. They said: "Who could have thought of making a masterpiece about arsonists? It's funny, witty and edgy. Article continues below "Visuals communicate firmly and directly to the audience. Smooth special effects. Excellent audio effects and background music. But it had been a while since Nicky and Simone Zimmermann had dropped into Los Angeles, where they opened their first-ever Stateside boutique back in 2011. (There are now some 92 standalone stores scattered across the globe.) Arriving to some very un-SoCal-like rain and flash flood warnings, the intense weather didn’t dampen the sisters’ perennially upbeat Aussie nature. Indeed, the bizarre conditions made for even more of a surreal and cinematic night at the fabled Chateau Marmont to celebrate the Twisted Romance-themed Cruise 2026 collection. Although rainwater was practically ricocheting off the neon sign erected poolside as a step-and-repeat photo moment, it didn’t deter guests from pulling their best blue steel poses, showing off their outfits for awaiting DJ-turned-photographer Myles Hendrik. As such, the best accessory of the evening proved to be a personal umbrella-wielding gentleman, ensuring no one slid right off the soaking wet tree-lined pathways. Once dried off indoors, attendees warmed up in glow of the Chateau’s candlelit bungalow over dirty martinis, glasses of Champagne, and deep belly laughter. Model Abby Champion, who has walked countless Zimmermann runways and recently wore a custom dress by Nicky Zimmermann during her wedding weekend , reunited with the Sydney-based designer. Longtime friends Emma Roberts, Dakota Fanning, and Zoey Deutch giggled together in a corner, while Jurnee Smollett introduced Halle Bailey to her older sister, Jazz. A long and languorous dinner unfolded at ethereal tables that nodded to the Twisted Romance mood. Ivory linens were laden with candelabras, deep burgundy-hued calla lilies, old silver coins, strings of pearls, and vintage glassware: an aesthetically-pleasing backdrop for crowd-favorite dishes like spicy tuna tartare, beetroot salad, Mediterranean branzino, and roasted chicken. “Tonight is about reconnecting with you all,” Nicky said, fresh from Paris where she splits her time to oversee the design atelier. “We haven't been going through LA as much as we used to, and we're lucky we get to see a lot of you around the world. Our first store in the US was on Robertson, which, like many things in our lives, came to us by chance and luck. We’ve now been in business nearly 35 years—which feels like a miracle! There’s a lot of stylists here, and we want you to know that your support is so meaningful and it has contributed a huge amount. We have always found LA, in particular, to be so supportive of us.” As anyone who owns a Zimmermann frock will tell you, they’re not pieces made for just sitting idle in. Before the last dinner fork had even hit the scallop-edged plate, guests were starting to make their way through the hotel to Penthouse 64 where the promise of dancing awaited. A corseted and ruffle-adorned Kitty Cash was already manning the DJ decks, and antique silver trays of espresso martinis were easily finding their way into outstretched hands. Actress Maria Bakalova was so relaxed, she was yapping cross-legged on the floor beside the fireplace, while the terrace became the place to grab both a chocolate madeline and a Vogue cigarette. With the rain pelting down on Sunset Boulevard and the wide open possibility of a Friday night ahead, there was simply no good reason to leave. Word travels fast too, as certain A listers who had been staying at the hotel for the GQ Men of the Year bash the night previous, caught wind and stopped by to hangout until well after 2 a.m. “I had no idea the Zimmermanns were this fun,” Rita Ora could be heard remarking. “It makes me love the clothes even more now.” Photo by: Myles Hendrik 1/18 Rita Ora Photo by: Myles Hendrik 2/18 Abby Champion, Larsen Thompson, Chloe East Photo by: Myles Hendrik 3/18 Beatrice Grannò Photo by: Myles Hendrik 4/18 Zoey Deutch, Dakota Fanning Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images 5/18 Emma Roberts More from Vogue Kate Middleton’s Dazzling Chandelier Earrings Are Steeped in Royal History Gather ’Round! text: Vogue World and Swarovski Honor Hollywood Skip to content Subscribe Main Navigation TV TV Ratings Reviews Movies Movies Steve Pond Reviews Box Office Venice Film Festival Report From Toronto Sundance Sundance Videos Cannes Cannes Magazine CinemaCon Awards Visionaries Awards Emmys Oscars How I Did It Venice Film Festival WrapStyle WrapStyle Homepage TheWrapBook Volume 4: The Art of Television 2025 TheWrapBook Volume 3: The Art of Cinema TheWrapBook Volume 2: The Art of Television TheWrapBook Volume 1: The Art of Cinema PRO Members Hub Data Insights Streaming Charts Waxword The Media Front Game On: A Wrap Sports Series The Grill WrapPRO What to Watch More Media Tech The Media Front Power Women Summit Screening Series RSVP Screenings Archive How She Did It How I Did It Digital Covers Newsletters Newsletters Search Search The Wrap Search Subscribe Follow Us Visit The Wrap on facebook Visit The Wrap on twitter Visit The Wrap on instagram Visit The Wrap on youtube Vogue World and Swarovski Honor Hollywood Costume’s Influence; Fashion’s FYC Season WrapStyle: This year’s Vogue event was a flex for the magazine and a long-overdue recognition of the influence film has on fashion Booth Moore October 31, 2025 @ 3:27 PM Share on Social Media Share on Facebook Share on X (formerly Twitter) Share on LinkedIn Share on Email Nicole Kidman walks the runway during Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26. Source: Getty Vogue World: Hollywood was a flex for the magazine and a long-overdue recognition of the influence film has on fashion. Also, Swarovski’s must-see “Masters of Light: Hollywood” exhibition of fashion and costume is on display and open to the public until Nov. 3. Greta Lee walks the runway during Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty Vogue World: Hollywood Is a Rah-Rah for the Fashion and Film Industries With Paramount Studios serving as a runway stage, Baz Luhrmann directing, a Chanel-clad Nicole Kidman starring, and a stacked celebrity cast and front row, Vogue World: Hollywood was a joyous mashup of fashion and film, featuring iconic Hollywood costumes, characters, fresh-off-the-runway fashion and archival looks. Say what you will about it being a pointless marketing exercise, and many online have said exactly that, but it was a rah-rah for both struggling industries, and a flex for Vogue, which is the only brand on the planet that could have pulled in all that star power. It also raised $4.5 million for the Entertainment Community Fund, providing a safety net for arts workers hit particularly hard this year. Sunday’s event brought 400-plus guests to the Paramount lot, including what were surely the most famous extras in history. “Picture’s up, places please, picture’s up!” a stage manager called over the bullhorn as they arrived on set. Miley Cyrus, Hailey Bieber and Anthony Vaccarello attend Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty “They’re stressing everybody out because we all actually do this and when you say picture’s up it’s serious!” Miley Cyrus said, walking in incognito wearing a Saint Laurent leather trench, newsboy cap and sunglasses. “I’m looking for the next motion picture star!” stylist Brad Goreski joked, looking every bit the studio boss in a dapper suit, sunglasses and slicked-back hair, arriving with Ashley Park in a corseted Wiederhoeft dress that carried a sense of costume. Brad Goreski and Ashley Park attend Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty Stars from music (Rita Ora, V, Machine Gun Kelly, Lizzo), film (Dakota Johnson, Gwyneth Paltrow, Cynthia Erivo, Taika Waititi), costume (Sandy Powell, Ruth E. Carter, Colleen Atwood), fashion (Anthony Vaccarello, Zac Posen, Jerry Lorenzo) and other power players in Anna Wintour’s orbit (Gov. Gavin Newsom, Bryan Lourd, Tyler Perry, Casey Wasserman) strolled past props, costume rails and spotlights on their way to director’s chair seats. The runway was high-energy and fast — people were having fun! — which is something we need more of in fashion and worked well for the 35-minute livestream of the show. While it was confusing to figure out what was designer-made and what was costume, that may have been the point. Damson Idris and Angela Bassett walk the runway at Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty The art forms have blurred. Costume designers have dipped their toes into fashion design and collaborated with luxury brands on films, not to mention continually influencing runway and street style decade after decade. Meanwhile, fashion designers are casting Hollywood faces as brand ambassadors, bringing even more showmanship to their runway shows and clothing to reach digital audiences, and even stepping into producing and costuming Hollywood films. All of it was on display on the runway. L.A.-based designers Kate and Laura Mulleavy were working in both worlds long before Anthony Vaccarello and Saint Laurent Films began producing awards-contending movies. They designed costumes for the 2010 film “Black Swan,” have cited the influence of films including “Suspiria” and “Star Wars” on many of their runway collections over the years, and made their own 2017 feature film, “Woodshock.” So it was fitting that several of their looks appeared on the Vogue World runway. Kendall Jenner wears a costume from “Moulin Rouge!,” a model wears a dress by Rodarte, Doja Cat wears a costume by Michael Schmidt inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome.” Source: Getty There used to be more of an impervious line between Hollywood costume and fashion; costume was for character building and serving a script, fashion was purely commercial. But all that’s gone out the window, as the relationship between Hollywood and fashion has become symbiotic. “In this era, people are able to step out of the boxes more and interact in the two fields simultaneously, and it’s accepted and celebrated,” Laura Mulleavy told me, noting that it was another polymath, Shirley Kurata, their longtime runway stylist and the costume designer for the 2022 film “Everything Everywhere All At Once,” who curated the evening’s contemporary character costumes. Jeff Goldblum walks the runway wearing Gucci at Vogue World. Source: Getty This recognition of costume designers’ contributions to visual culture — and to fashion, including countless collection mood boards — was long overdue. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve previewed a collection with a fashion designer who talks about being inspired by a particular film without naming, or even knowing, the costume designer. Hopefully, that mindset will start to change. The photo below says it all about the flow of creativity and reference from one world to the other — Wintour poses with costume designer Mona May and her iconic yellow plaid suit, as worn by Alicia Silverstone in the 1995 film “Clueless,” alongside a checked suit in the same spirit by fashion designer Thom Browne. Left to right, a model wears Thom Browne, costume designer Mona May, Condé Nast Chief Content Director Anna Wintour and a Mona May-designed costume from Clueless. Source: Getty There was a lot to look at on the runway. Some of the highlights: Kendall Jenner as a “Moulin Rouge!” showgirl in a leggy look from costume designer Catherine Martin, and “Great Gatsby” flappers — including Elizabeth Debicki — wearing beaded gowns Martin created for the 2013 film in collaboration with Prada. The tribute to the late, great style icon Diane Keaton and her influential “Annie Hall” look was not only touching but telling of how costume and fashion can intersect. It was originally developed by Keaton in 1977 with costume designer Ruth Morley, using some pieces from her personal wardrobe and some from Ralph Lauren, who recreated the look for the runway here, and has referenced it many times in his fashion collections over the years. There were also homages to the unforgettable costumes of “The Royal Tenenbaums” (Karen Patch), “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” (Arianne Phillips) and “Edward Scissorhands” (Colleen Atwood). Elizabeth Debicki wallks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Angela Bassett closed the Afrofuturism section looking regal in her Ruth E. Carter gown on the heels of dancing “Black Panther” Wakandan warriors. Greta Lee worked a theatrical look and tricorne hat from fashion/costume designer Jonathan Anderson’s first Dior collection shown just weeks ago. Jeff Goldblum owned his Gucci sequin jacket and his runway walk, and Julia Garner skipped down the runway as the picture of baroque frivolity in a Milena Canonero for “Marie Antoinette” costume. Julia Garner walks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Gracie Abrams played the part of Chanel ambassador, performing in a fresh-off-the-runway look by Matthieu Blazy, while Doja Cat shook her hips in a chainmail dress inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome,” but executed by L.A.’s Michael Schmidt, a too-often unsung hero of costume design and fabrication. It was a blast and nobody wanted it to end. On the way out, I ran into “Frankenstein” costume designer Kate Hawley, whose ravishing work, including curating Tiffany & Co. archival jewels and custom pieces for the film, is proof that the love affair between costume and fashion isn’t ending anytime soon. Costume designers Mona May, Sandy Powell, Catherine Martin, Ruth E. Carter, Arianne Phillips, Milena Canonero, Jacqueline West, Shirley Kurata with Anna Wintour at Vogue World: Hollywood. Source: Getty Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood” Source: Swarovski Fashion’s FYC Season Brands have descended on L.A. in what I’m calling fashion’s FYC (For Your Consideration) period in the lead-up to awards season. Everything from Boucheron jewels and hot-off-the-runway Versace to designer Camilla Franks’ fun, rock ’n’ roll resortwear and Le Monde Beryl’s red-carpet-ready silk pumps is being showcased for celebrities and stylists at spectacular events, rented hotel rooms and showrooms across the city. The goal? To create media moments, build relationships and make deals as opportunities to dress up, ramp up over the next few months. Swarovski joined the chorus Tuesday, asserting its role as chief embellisher of fashion and film. Global creative director Giovanna Engelbert and CEO Alexis Nasard hosted the opening of the Swarovski “Masters of Light” immersive exhibition — following stops in Vienna, Milan, Shanghai and Seoul — curated by Alexander Fury with a Hollywood focus for this edition. Unlike most fashion happenings, this is open to the public, through Nov. 3 in the former Amoeba Music space. Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie designed gown worn by Marilyn Monroe on display at Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Cher, Viola Davis, Kylie Jenner, Elizabeth Olsen, Jeff Goldblum and many more turned out for the sparkly opening, exploring galleries showcasing Swarovski’s 130 year history of bedazzling fashion, jewelry, home decor and more. The brand has a century-long history in Hollywood, from lighting up Dorothy’s ruby red slippers in “The Wizard of Oz” (there’s a pair in the exhibition), to creating the jewels worn by Marilyn Monroe in “Gentlemen Prefer Blondes” (also here), to partnering with the Academy Awards, and on many a costume and red carpet dress. Like Vogue World, the exhibition is a conversation between fashion and costume — and full of eye candy — including the Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie-designed nude illusion dress worn by Monroe when she sang “Happy Birthday” to President John F. Kennedy, and by Kim Kardashian to the Met Gala, which had its own velvet-roped vestibule. Cher and Giovanna Battaglia Engelbert at the opening of Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Demonstrating how costumes have inspired fashion, Travis Banton’s gold silk, glass bead, bullion, crystal and mink “Fabergé” dress — said to be one of the most expensive ever produced by Paramount and worn by Marlene Dietrich in the 1937 film “Angel” — is displayed next to a 2024 Marc Jacobs gown inspired by it. “Masters of Light” offers a window into the brand’s craft and design process in vivid color, and many more show stopping looks, including Josephine Baker’s incredible metal and crystal bra and feather costume from “La Revue Nègre,” Katy Perry’s iconic Jeremy Scott chandelier dress, a crystallized Harry Styles jumpsuit and more worn by Cher, Madonna, Grace Jones, Beyoncé, Tina Turner, Carey Mulligan and more. Tickets can be purchased here . Left, Travis Banton’s “Fabergé” dress from the 1937 film Angel, and right, the 2024 Marc Jacobs dress it inspired. Source: Swarovski Valérie Messika and Orlando Bloom at the Messika celebratory dinner at The Frick Collection in New York. Source: Messika Sparkling from Coast to Coast Meanwhile in New York, Messika jewelry celebrated its 20th anniversary, and the opening of a new Madison Avenue flagship, with a glittering dinner at The Frick Collection bringing together a cross-section of celebrities, fashion insiders and friends of the brand. More than 120 guests, including Julianne Moore, Charlotte Lawrence, Nina Dobrev, Kiko Mizuhara, Orlando Bloom, and Gunna, gathered in the museum’s galleries for an evening that blended haute joaillerie and haute cuisine. In a clever twist, models dressed as servers and glided through the dining room in a trompe-l’œil performance, revealing Messika’s high jewelry pieces as they moved. Messika celebratory dinner at The Frick Collection in New York City. Source: Messika The centerpiece was the So Move Rainbow High Jewelry set, with 24 sapphire shades and rubies created exclusively for the new boutique. Rainbow hues ran throughout the event — from the photo call backdrop to the table settings to the anniversary cake. Produced by We Are Ona, known for its immersive culinary events, the dinner featured a custom menu by Chef Alexia Duchêne, and culminated in a soulful performance by Toni Braxton. “This opening is more than a milestone,” Valérie Messika, who founded the modern jewelry brand in Paris in 2005, said. “It’s a bridge between Paris and New York, between savoir-faire and emotion, and the beginning of a luminous new chapter for Messika in the United States.” Laura Brown, Laura Dern, Kristina O’Neill and Cindy Crawford celebrate “All The Cool Girls Get Fired” at the Tory Burch store. Source: Tory Burch All The Cool Girls… Former magazine editors Laura Brown and Kristina O’Neill have been crisscrossing the country with their new book, “All The Cool Girls Get Fired,” which I had the pleasure of interviewing them about onstage at Reese Witherspoon’s Shine Away event a couple weekends back. It’s a timely read for people who, ahem, have been laid off, with personal anecdotes from Oprah, Katie Couric, Jamie Lee Curtis and others, as well as practical advice about COBRA and mental health — all the fun stuff. Zoey Deutch, Jurnee Smollett and Monica Lewinsky read excerpts from “All the Cool Girls Get Fired.” Source: Tory Burch The authors were back in L.A. last week for a party at the Tory Burch store where Kiernan Shipka, Lake Bell, Jurnee Smollett and others took turns reading excerpts from the book. Monica Lewinsky stole the show, however, with her introduction: “I don’t mean to show anyone up, but I was fired from the White House!” I asked guests for their getting-fired stories. Burch has never been fired (of course she hasn’t). Cindy Crawford was asked to leave a Bruce Weber shoot once, but models don’t get fired so much as they don’t get booked, she said. Stylist/manager/producer Jeanne Yang was fired from her job as a salesperson in the Bullocks Wilshire lingerie department way back when, which led her to Details magazine and eventually to styling—a good thing in retrospect. Critics Choice Super Awards to Air This Weekend Sammi Turano November 12, 2025 Originally posted on January 6, 2021 @ 5:00 pm The Critics Choice Association (CCA) announced today the incredible line-up of talent that will join hosts Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the inaugural Critics Choice Super Awards , helping them to honor the most popular, fan-obsessed genres across both television and movies, including Superhero/Comic Book, Science Fiction/Fantasy, Horror, Action and Animation. Shohreh Aghdashloo, Aya Cash, Madelyn Cline, Mike Colter, Colman Domingo, Tom Ellis, Courtney Ford, Tiffany Haddish, Sam Heughan, Maddison Jaizani, Lennie James, Martin Kove, Javicia Leslie, Leah Lewis, Caity Lotz, Ralph Macchio, Kennedy McMann, Elizabeth Mitchell, Lindsey Morgan, Bob Morley, Genevieve Padalecki, Jared Padalecki, Brandon Routh, Chase Stokes, Eliza Taylor, Gina Torres, Alan Tudyk, and William Zabka, will all serve as presenters during the special ceremony, which will air on The CW Network on Sunday, January 10, 2021 (8:00-10:00pm ET/PT) and will stream the next day for free on The CW App and cwtv.com. “We know that the Super Awards are in the best hands with Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the helm,” said Critics Choice Association CEO Joey Berlin. “They bring with them an unparalleled knowledge of and enthusiasm for these sometimes underappreciated genres that we know fans and viewers will love. They are joined by a stellar line-up of fan favorites who will be on hand to support their ‘Super’ colleagues and help showcase the very best in popular entertainment.” The Critics Choice Association will also present the Legacy Award to the “Star Trek” franchise, recognizing the cultural impact it has had across multiple decades while continuing to appeal to and grow its loyal fanbase with new stories and characters. “Star Trek” icon Patrick Stewart , and “Star Trek: Discovery” trailblazer Sonequa Martin-Green will personally accept this special honor, which comes as the franchise celebrates its 55 th anniversary. See also Critics Choice Association to Honor Harrison Ford Hulu and NEON’s “Palm Springs” leads this year’s film nominees, with a total of five including Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Andy Samberg, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie and Best Villain in a Movie for J.K. Simmons, and Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Cristin Milioti. Several films followed close behind with four nominations including “Birds of Prey” (Warner Bros.), “Freaky” (Universal), “Onward” (Disney+), “Sonic the Hedgehog” (Paramount), “The Hunt” (Universal), “The Old Guard” (Netflix), and “The Willoughbys” (Netflix). “Lovecraft Country” (HBO) received the most television nominations, with a total of six possible wins, including Best Horror Series, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Jonathan Majors, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Michael K. Williams, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Wunmi Mosaku, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Jurnee Smollett, and Best Villain in a Series for Abbey Lee. Amazon’s “The Boys” received five nominations including Best Superhero/Comic Book Series, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series and Best Villain in a Series for Antony Starr, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Karl Urban, and Best Actress in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Aya Cash. For the full list of nominees, and additional information, visit: https://www.criticschoice.com/critics-choice-super-awards/ Kevin Smith has been saying silly cinematic shit since 1994’s “Clerks.” 2021 marks the 27 th year since the last time he had a real job. A polygamist, he’s married to both his wife, Jen, and podcasting. Writer, comedian, and actress Dani Fernandez is a frequent speaker at San Diego Comic Con, LA Comic Con, and New York Comic Con and has been a panelist for The CW’s “Crisis Aftermath.” She has hosted for E!, Disney, Nerdist, Skybound, Funimation, and iHeartRadio, among others. She can currently be seen on Syfy’s “The Great Debate” and in Disney’s “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” playing herself. She is also an accomplished television writer with credits at Netflix and HBO Max. See also Shirley Wins SOFEE The inaugural Critics Choice Super Awards show will be produced by Bob Bain Productions. The CCA is represented by Dan Black of Greenberg Traurig. Search site Submit search Subscribe Newsletter Advertise News & City Arts & Entertainment Food & Drink Life & Style Events Sports Top Professionals Awards Travel Newsletter Sign Up Advertise News & City Arts & Entertainment Food & Drink Life & Style Events Sports Top Professionals Awards Travel Search Search site Submit search Honoree Jamie Lee Curtis and Presenter Jane Fonda Get Political at WIF Honors Gala Plus, Kristen Wiig is named an ‘Icon’ and Maude Apatow received the 20th WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award Jasmin Rosemberg • November 7, 2025 Jane Fonda presents Jamie Lee Curtis the Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award at the 2025 WIF Honors presented by Max Mara Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF “For the last five years, I’ve been lucky enough to present the Women In Film Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award,” began Jane Fonda after receiving a standing ovation in the Beverly Hilton ballroom at the WIF Honors event presented by Max Mara on Nov. 6. “[I present it] to a woman in the entertainment industry who demonstrates brave commitment to humanitarian issues, and is woke,” she said, to laughs. She pulled back her maroon Max Mara blazer to reveal a black T-shirt with the word, “resist.” Fonda continued: “I realized, given today’s reality, humanitarianism and empathy are essential forms of resistance. … It’s at the heart of what we do in our profession, empathy. And you know what else is at the heart of what we do? The First Amendment. Our profession, like all art forms, can’t exist without freedom of expression. It’s the bedrock of democracy, and it’s being taken away from us. And that’s why, on Oct. 1, we launched the Committee for the First Amendment .” Fonda clarified the Committee was re-launched, as it existed in the ’70’s and ’80s, when her father was a member. “But dig this,” she said. “That was about one small part of government robbing us of our First Amendment. Right now, it’s the entire federal government. It is far, far worse than what existed back in the ’40s and ’50s. And so, we have to do something about that.” Then she praised the recipient of this year’s Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. “Jamie Lee Curtis and I have a few things in common,” Fonda said. “We’re both children of major movie stars and we made our own way quite successfully in their business. And we’re both late bloomers — which is okay. It moves me very deeply to see how Jamie uses her skills and her remarkable ego-less courage as an actor. … And last January, when the fires were burning and our hearts were breaking, I heard Jamie Lee Curtis had given a million dollars to the fire department and it made me cry.” Fonda added how Curtis had also raised millions of dollars for Children’s Hospital L.A., and has used her voice for addiction and trans rights. When she took the stage, Curtis also spoke about government. “I heard it today that she is retiring from public service, and I thought this Women In Film crowd could just give Nancy Pelosi a loud [round of applause]. … What an example to me of a life of service!” She also professed: “I am most excited to stand here two days after the repudiation of the authoritative regime. The election of these two beautiful women to governorships.” Curtis thanked her presenter. “Jane Fonda, I have watched you in wonder and shock and awe, at the way that you walk through the world as an artist, as an activist and as a disruptor in residence.” She noted that she joined the Committee of the First Amendment. Credit: hoto by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Then she recalled the birth of her activism. “My mother, the late, great, Janet Leigh,” Curtis said, getting tearful, “was an actress with an impressive career. But she knew there was much more to be done with fame.” She described how a group of seven women whose husbands were in entertainment (including Gloria Franks and Jeanne Martin) came together to use their positions to help children and form SHARE (Share Happily And Reap Endlessly), which her mother joined. “For 70 years, the group has raised over $70 million for children,” said Curtis, who has fond memories of helping in their events as a child. Getting emotional again, she added, “I know that my mother would be so very proud that her life and her work made an impact on mine.” Curtis told the audience how, on Dec. 12, Disney is releasing Ella McKay. “It’s about the rise of an idealistic young woman,” she said, “but it’s also a movie about politics.” She ended by citing the last line of the narration of the movie, which she stars in. “‘There is no opposite word for trauma, but hope comes close,'” Curtis read. “And today, I feel hope.” WIF CEO Kirsten Schaffer also acknowledged today’s difficult climate. “There is no doubt that there are people in positions of great power who would like to erase us: Erase our impact, silence our voices, diminish our power, keep us quiet and small and ineffective,” she said. “But we are not small. We are seldom quiet. And we are definitely effective.” WIF’s mission is to advance equity and representation across the screen industries. The WIF Honors gala — which celebrates female storytellers and change-makers who are making their mark on culture through their art and advocacy — raises funds for WIF’s education, career development and advocacy programs. Other sponsors of this year’s event included e.l.f. Cosmetics, Amazon MGM Studios, Apple TV, Delta Air Lines, Disney, Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey P. Horvath, Netflix and STARZ #TakeTheLead. Karen Pittman, wearing Max Mara, Davida Lara, Regina King, wearing Max Mara, Roda Ahmed, Mara Brock Akil, wearing Max Mara, and Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Next, Karen Pittman honored Forever ’s Mara Brock Akil, Judy Blume (who accepted via video) and Regina King with the Crystal Award for Advocacy in TV. “What woman has not read Judy Blume?” said King during a conversation. “You become a writer as a reader first, and I devoured every book that she had,” added Akil. Maria Bello, the first recipient of the WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award, called up other past recipients — Lili Reinhart (2022), Elizabeth Debicki (2019) and Zoey Deutch (2017) — in celebration of the award’s 20th anniversary. Elizabeth Debicki, Lili Reinhart, Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti, Maude Apatow, Zoey Deutch and Maria Bello, all wearing Max Mara with Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF attend the 2025 WIF Honors presented by Max Mara Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Then, Maude Apatow received the 20th WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award from Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti, whose grandfather founded Max Mara 75 years ago. Max Mara has supported the WIF Honors event since the beginning, and dressed 2025 attendees included King, Curtis, Fonda, Pittman, Apatow, Mara Brock Akil, Gabrielle Nadig, Atsuko Okatsuka, Janicza Bravo, Reinhart, Deutch, Debicki, Bello, Jurnee Smollett, Leslie Mann, Maggie Kang and Beth Reisgraf. “When I was 10, I read Are You There, God? It’s Me Margaret, ” said Apatow, shouting out Blume. “It was funny, angsty, truthful and made me fall in love with reading.” The actor and director then called out another female influence. “As a teenager, I got to watch a 20-something-year-old Lena Dunham write, direct, act and produce a truly groundbreaking show,” she said of Girls , produced by her father, Judd Apatow. She added, “But my favorite woman in film is my mom, Leslie Mann.” Francesca Amiker, Tessa Thompson, Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig, wearing Max Mara, speak onstage at the 2025 WIF Honors Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Janicza Bravo presented the the Crystal Award for Advocacy in Film award to Hedda ’s Tessa Thompson, Nia DaCosta (not present), Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig. Lastly, Kaia Gerber honored her Palm Royale co-star Kristen Wiig with the inaugural Icon Award. “Who better to receive it than my favorite scene partner?” Gerber said. “For seven years at SNL , Kristen showed us comedy could be completely unhinged and utterly ‘stupid’ — a word I learned from Kristen herself as one of the highest forms of praise in comedy — and also, somehow be simultaneously deeply human.” Kaia Gerber, Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF and Icon Award recipient Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Gerber continued, “When Bridesmaids came out, it was a revelation. … There is such truth and utter heartbreak behind [all of her characters].” She finished, “Tonight, we celebrate the woman who taught us that comedy is art, that chaos is beautiful, that sheer stupidity is not only encouraged but a necessity of life and that being unapologetically yourself might just be the most iconic move of all.” An emotional Wiig thanked Gerber, who she called “a lighthouse” on her show. “I’m fully overwhelmed,” she said. “This is my first time having to make a speech like this. I just kept thinking, ‘How did I get here?’ … I keep coming back to the people who said ‘yes’ to me before I had anything on my resume.” Wiig noted how her whole life changed when she joined The Groundlings. “That led to SNL ,” she said. She called out two men: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow (who reached out to her and asked if she wanted to write something). “I certainly wouldn’t be up here getting an award from Women In Film if it weren’t for that movie,” she said of the project that changed her life. Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF But ultimately, she’s enjoyed collaborating with women and exploring female characters. “I just love stories about women,” Wiig said. “We’re so crazy! We’re complex. We talk to each other about how we age, and our sensitivities and our intuition. It’s a never-ending source of material. I want to keep going,” she pledged. “I want to keep telling stories about women, with women.” Wiig then offered everyone a challenge. “I still have things in my career that I really want to do — that I’m really scared to do,” she confessed. “And so I just thought, by chance, if everyone in this room has that thing that they’ve really wanted to do or really been scared to do — maybe we make like a collective pact with each other that we’re going to just do it, anyway.” Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! She pulled back her maroon Max Mara blazer to reveal a black T-shirt with the word, “resist. ” Fonda continued: “I realized, given today’s reality, humanitarianism and empathy are essential forms of resistance. … It’s at the heart of what we do in our profession, empathy. And you know what else is at the heart of what we do? The First Amendment. Our profession, like all art forms, can’t exist without freedom of expression. It’s the bedrock of democracy, and it’s being taken away from us. And that’s why, on Oct. 1, we launched the Committee for the First Amendment. ” Fonda clarified the Committee was re-launched, as it existed in the ’70’s and ’80s, when her father was a member. “But dig this,” she said. “That was about one small part of government robbing us of our First Amendment. Right now, it’s the entire federal government. It is far, far worse than what existed back in the ’40s and ’50s. And so, we have to do something about that. ” Then she praised the recipient of this year’s Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. “Jamie Lee Curtis and I have a few things in common,” Fonda said. “We’re both children of major movie stars and we made our own way quite successfully in their business. And we’re both late bloomers — which is okay. It moves me very deeply to see how Jamie uses her skills and her remarkable ego-less courage as an actor. … And last January, when the fires were burning and our hearts were breaking, I heard Jamie Lee Curtis had given a million dollars to the fire department and it made me cry. ” Fonda added how Curtis had also raised millions of dollars for Children’s Hospital L. , and has used her voice for addiction and trans rights. When she took the stage, Curtis also spoke about government. “I heard it today that she is retiring from public service, and I thought this Women In Film crowd could just give Nancy Pelosi a loud [round of applause]. … What an example to me of a life of service!” She also professed: “I am most excited to stand here two days after the repudiation of the authoritative regime. The election of these two beautiful women to governorships. ” Curtis thanked her presenter. “Jane Fonda, I have watched you in wonder and shock and awe, at the way that you walk through the world as an artist, as an activist and as a disruptor in residence. ” She noted that she joined the Committee of the First Amendment.
